answer: A fresh agent must earn three certifications from established peers before its identity can bridge into the honest kernel of the trust graph. Sybil farms only attest each other, so their cluster stays isolated across a trust canyon from that kernel. Kernel-anchored ranking like SybilRank runs random walks whose trust flow decays exponentially when crossing the canyon, pinning fake accounts near zero. The cost to an attacker: every unearned bridge demands compromising a real peer or waiting out years of honest history. Most bots quit long before that.
